name: The Turnaround Firm
tagline: Join cash diagnosis to a bounded, testable recovery sprint.
mission: Bring finance, product recovery, engineering, operations, and customer success together around a distressed fictional subscription business. Reconcile the original synthetic financials, reproduce a real small dispatch defect, and plan a constrained recovery sprint without claiming realized savings or customer outcomes.

teams.name: Finance and Runway
teams.purpose: Reconcile cash, reserve unpaid obligations, and separate scenario arithmetic from realized results.

teams.name: Product Recovery
teams.purpose: Connect support impact, scope, priority rules, and the final hold/rework decision.

teams.name: Engineering Recovery
teams.purpose: Reproduce and repair the authored priority-sorting defect with narrow regression coverage.

teams.name: Operations
teams.purpose: Create capacity-bounded support work, validate handoff behavior, and retain blocked/deferred work.

teams.name: Customer Success
teams.purpose: Prepare truthful, approval-gated response drafts and avoid unearned commitments or fabricated resolution claims.

case.title: Cedarline Desk: cash containment and a broken support dispatch queue
case.brief: SYNTHETIC case at 2026-09-30: Cedarline Desk has declining subscription receipts, increasing refunds, USD 32400 closing cash, and twelve authored open tickets. Its actual small reference dispatcher alphabetizes severity, sending low-priority tickets ahead of urgent ones. A five-day planning sprint has 360 engineering minutes and 420 support-remediation minutes. No production account, money, trade, customer message, or realized recovery is involved.
success_criteria: Fifteen synthetic cash rows reconcile USD 52000 opening cash plus USD 48500 receipts less USD 68100 payments to USD 32400 closing cash.
USD 5500 incremental prior-period payables are reserved separately; runway to the USD 12000 floor is about 49.7 days under the repeated-September scenario.
The alphabetical dispatch defect is reproducible and a candidate policy prioritizes eligible urgent tickets without dispatching a blocked ticket.
The support simulation selects six tickets totaling exactly 420 estimated minutes and retains all other tickets as blocked or deferred.
Any proposed USD 1700 monthly containment difference remains an approval-dependent scenario, not achieved savings, profit, sales, or executed financial activity.

tasks.title: Reconcile the three-month cash and subscription baseline
tasks.instructions: Run the authored analysis utility and tests, reconcile every synthetic transaction to monthly plan counts, and distinguish cash receipts from general revenue-recognition claims.
acceptance: Reproduces opening 52000, receipts 48500, payments 68100, and closing 32400 USD.
Reports monthly net cash of -4000, -6600, and -9000 USD with the explicit fixture assumption that subscription billings were collected in-month.
Keeps incremental unpaid prior-period obligations outside the cash-ledger payments.

tasks.title: Map the authored backlog to recovery risk
tasks.instructions: Review ticket severity, age, affected-account counts, and dependencies. Do not sum overlapping affected-account counts into unique customers or assert that a support fix recovers revenue.
acceptance: Covers twelve open tickets, four urgent rows, and the one blocked urgent ticket.
Connects the dispatch behavior to delayed urgent work without inventing churn attribution or actual customer harm.

tasks.title: Reproduce severity alphabetization in the reference dispatcher
tasks.instructions: Run the small authored product dispatcher through the analysis utility and create a minimal reproduction. Keep this baseline fixture separate from any candidate fix.
acceptance: Shows the legacy first four as ticket-009, ticket-002, ticket-006, and ticket-012, all low priority.
Explains why string sorting places low before normal before urgent and shows the blocked row is excluded.

tasks.title: Set runway and authority guardrails
tasks.instructions: Reserve the prior-period catch-up obligations and compute the repeated-September runway to zero and to the owner's cash floor. Specify review triggers and prohibit automatic spending or cost actions.
acceptance: Reserves USD 5500 and reports USD 26900 available before the USD 12000 floor.
Reports approximately 89.7 days to zero after reserves and 49.7 days to the floor using 30-day modeled months.
Does not treat these mechanical scenarios as a forecast guarantee, solvency opinion, trade, or authorized financial action.

tasks.title: Agree the narrow recovery triage rule
tasks.instructions: Define severity ranking, oldest-first ties, blocked exclusions, deterministic identifiers, and capacity handling. Reconcile the policy with cash and customer-risk constraints before changing code.
acceptance: Orders eligible urgent before normal before low; same-severity work is oldest first with deterministic ties.
Defines the non-preemptive fit rule and records that a larger deferred ticket is not silently completed or discarded.

tasks.title: Plan the 420-minute support slice
tasks.instructions: Run the candidate triage simulation under the approved-for-review policy and map the chosen work to the five-day sprint skeleton. Keep blocked and capacity-deferred tickets visible.
acceptance: Selects ticket-001, ticket-010, ticket-007, ticket-011, ticket-005, and ticket-008 for exactly 420 estimated minutes.
Retains one blocked and five capacity-deferred tickets; it reports no actual completion or resolution.
Keeps the separate 360-minute engineering budget distinct from support capacity.

tasks.title: Produce a minimal dispatcher candidate
tasks.instructions: Implement the agreed severity ranking in a candidate module with narrow tests. Preserve the authored defective baseline as reproduction evidence; do not deploy or execute work against real accounts.
acceptance: Rejects unknown severities and invalid limits, excludes blocked/non-open work, and handles ties deterministically.
Returns ticket-001, ticket-010, ticket-007, and ticket-011 for the agreed four-item review batch.
Makes no network, persistence, customer, or billing changes.

tasks.title: Verify candidate queue behavior and rollback boundaries
tasks.instructions: Execute the candidate's tests and replay the acceptance table against both the preserved baseline and candidate. Review capacity accounting and explain how an owner could hold the candidate without changing the reference.
acceptance: Separates the intentionally failing legacy behavior from candidate pass/fail evidence.
Records blocked-ticket, zero-capacity, duplicate-ID, deterministic-tie, and unknown-severity cases.
Explicitly says production deployment and support execution have not occurred.

tasks.title: Prepare honest customer-response drafts
tasks.instructions: Adapt the supplied response policy into incident-class drafts and a review routing sheet. Refer only to synthetic ticket IDs and avoid promises of resolution time, refunds, recovered money, or completed fixes.
acceptance: Covers urgent export failure, blocked reproduction, and low-priority cosmetic feedback with different truthful next steps.
Labels every draft unsent and requires owner review before any actual customer communication or refund commitment.

tasks.title: Model containment without claiming savings
tasks.instructions: Compare the repeated-September scenario to the supplied lower contractor/hosting assumption. Explain the approval and operational evidence needed, using regression results as a constraint rather than treating them as achieved financial value.
acceptance: Shows USD 9000 versus USD 7300 modeled monthly burn, a USD 1700 difference, and the associated cash-floor sensitivity.
Marks contractor and hosting changes unapproved and includes no actual cancellation, transfer, purchase, sale, trade, or profit claim.

tasks.title: Issue the bounded recovery decision
tasks.instructions: Join cash diagnosis, candidate quality, the capacity plan, response drafts, and containment scenarios into a hold/rework/candidate recommendation. Document what new evidence is needed after any separately approved sprint.
acceptance: Names unresolved risks, baseline/candidate differences, and a measurement plan for real future work.
Claims no realized profit, completed customer recovery, live deployment, or external authority.
